utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-67-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. May I have the appearances. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff and Ulrich Mussemeyer, and we are accompanied by Ana Katalinic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff. For the Defence. I see, Mr. Seselj, that you're here, you represent yourself and stand-by counsel, Mr. Van der Spoel is present as well. That's on the record then. We are having a Status Conference to check on the status of the case and to make some announcements. Mr. Seselj, I made a very brief list of matters that I would like to deal with. I usually do it very shortly before the Status Conference, but since I have a translation for you, it could be handed out as a courtesy copy. If in future moments I would have such a list available and if there's sufficient time to communicate that to you, I'll try do that so that you're better able to prepare. Mr. Seselj, the first item on the agenda after an introduction is your health and your conditions of detention. Mr. Seselj, I'd like to give you an opportunity to raise any issue in relation to your health, and if you wish it could be done in private session. If this's anything to be raised as far as detention conditions are concerned, you may do so as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, I'm never going to ask for private session for any matter, especially not with respect to my condition of health. On the 7th of June, I sent you, as the Trial Chamber, a submission on just five pages, normal five pages, normal format, and I presented there basic information about my health. This was prepared by members of my expert team, and there are an additional three pages with the original medical finding, medical report, by a cardiology, pulmologist [as interpreted], and neurosurgeon. You, Mr. Orie, returned that to me, returned my submission probably because the explanation you gave was that I hadn't counted the correct number of words. And in your ruling and decision you called my legal experts "so-called experts," which is an insult. They are my real experts and my real expert team for preparing my defence. Therefore, Mr. Orie, I have decided not to give you any information in future with respect to my health condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then, any matter in relation to detention conditions, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I recently received a package, a travelling bag with clothing which contained T-shirts, caps, socks, jerseys, and so on, and goodness knows what else, with Serbian national symbols and insignia. And it says with the slogan "Serbia is rooting for you," with respect to the world football championships. But the authorities in the Detention Unit did not allow me to receive that package and seized it. That kind of conduct is broadly tolerated for all the other inmates, the Croats have T-shirts with enormous national insignia and so on, but it has been denied me. Even during the football championships the guards wore Dutch T-shirts rooting for the Dutch national team. I think this is serious discrimination which cannot be tolerated. So they are not propagating my party, my alleged crimes, myself as a public figure, but the clothing just had national emblems, the national emblems of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, have you addressed the Registrar on the matter?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, there's absolutely no sense for me to address the Registrar on any matter, and I wouldn't have presented that matter here either to you had you not asked me about the conditions of detention. That is another subject that I'm not going to raise at any occasion. But since you asked me, I presented it here and now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Seselj, you know the rules. The rules are that it's the registry -- the Registrar who's responsible for the situation in the Detention Unit, but if any matter in the Detention Unit would have an impact on the proceedings in this courtroom, then after you have addressed the Registrar, you can address the Chamber, but the Chamber, neither I as a Pre-Trial Judge, is going to take over the responsibilities of the Registrar. So within the limits I just explained to you, you can address the Chamber. Mr. Seselj, having dealt with both what you told me about health issues and about the package of clothing you insist that you should have received, anything else on the first agenda item?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move on to the next agenda item, which is disclosure. Earlier today, Mr. Seselj, I issued, or the Chamber issued the decision on the format of disclosure. You'll receive it translated as soon as possible, but meanwhile I already could read to the parties the disposition so that you are at least informed about the bulk of the decision. Let me just find it. The disposition reads as follows - of course the original written decision being authoritative - that the Trial Chamber finds that the Prosecution is entitled to provide Rule 66(A) and (B) material as well as Rule 68(i) material in electronic format subject to the qualifications regarding assistance for the accused. The Trial Chamber also finds that there is an obligation to provide Rule 68(i) material in a language the accused understands. The Trial Chamber directs the Prosecution to provide the accused with those witness statements in its possession in which the accused is mentioned by name, subject to the exceptions mentioned in the body of the decision. Further, the Trial Chamber directs the Prosecution to provide the accused with the names or pseudonyms and transcript references of private and closed session testimony in cases before this Tribunal where the accused is mentioned by name. Further details you'll find in the decision. Then the Chamber dismisses all other requests in the aforementioned filings by the parties, and the Chamber also dismisses all other motions of the accused for translation of material into Serbo-Croatian to the extent that they are inconsistent with the present decision. This decision has been signed, is -- will be translated and will be given to you, but you're already aware, Mr. Seselj, of what the decision is about. That's the decision on the disclosure. I'd like to pay attention at this moment to the status of the disclosure so far. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, one clarification. In the past we have actually tried to disclose electronic versions of all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- these materials. Is that -- do we have to repeat it or is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I will read you the relevant part of the decision in that respect. Now I just hope that I've got the -- the -- The decision contains a paragraph on compliance, which -- and I'm now putting it very short, says that if the accused, if Mr. Seselj refuses to accept any electronic disclosure, that -- so if he refuses to accept that material, then you would have discharged your obligations in this respect. But it also says that if Mr. Seselj would decide that after all he accepts the material, he's entitled to receive it, including material he has refused to accept in the past. So it should be offered to him again upon request, as the decision says, of the accused, this must be provided anew to him by the Prosecution. So specific attention is paid to that aspect in the decision. Then I'd like to move on to the status of disclosure so far. And of course I'm aware that the -- the fact that the decision of the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have something to say, Mr. Orie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll first -- one second. I'll find a moment soon where you have an opportunity to say something. I first would like to inquire into the first material that's 66(A)(i), the supporting material. The current status is -- as I understand is completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And if you like to hear more details, Mr. Mussemeyer is prepared to give you all the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the last batch of disclosure was done on the 26th of January of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Seselj, would you like to say anything in respect of this agenda item, that's disclosure under 66(A)(i)?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, since the Prosecutor had a question, I have a question, too, just one single question. What am I to do, Mr. Orie, with those computer diskettes that the Prosecutor is going to provide me with? On the one hand, you have forbidden me to send material to my legal advisors; and on the other hand, you are making me take it in electronic format, which is quite useless to me. And I take advantage of this opportunity to make a request that you issue me a request for an appeal to the Appeals Chamber, because if I send in my request in writing you might return it to me because the correct number of words is not there and I haven't counted them properly, whereas it is in the interests of justice that you assign a court official who will count the words himself and look through the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, you are raising a few questions. You say: What to do with the computer diskettes? I would say use them and the decision says something about support you would receive in order to be able to use that material. Within the limits of other decisions, of course you can share knowledge, but strictly within the limits of other decisions, with whomever is entitled to share that information with you. Finally, Mr. Seselj, whether or not you want to look at that material is entirely in your own hands. You just addressed to me the request that I should assign a court official to do the word count. The answer is that I will not assign any court official to do the word count for you. You have to do that yourself. If you want to appeal the decision of the Chamber, you know the procedure to follow; that is, you should apply for a certificate for an appeal and give the reasons for it. I advise you to take into consideration what the Rules say about the criteria, and then the Chamber will decide on the matter. Then I'd like to move on to the present state of disclosure in relation to Rule 66(A)(ii). Could the Prosecution say whether there's anything new on that. I remember that on the 19th of May, he was referring to: "If a decision is issued soon regarding the Trial Chamber's appropriate form for disclosure, then we expect very soon to be able to begin disclosure of additional witness statements under Rule 66(A)(ii)." And if you are permitted, as he said, to make this disclosure in electronic form, you expect to be able to complete this work no later than the end of July. That is what was said on the 19th of May. Is there anything to add to that at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there's nothing to add. We can immediately begin our disclosure for all the witnesses who are not sensitive. We already have burned their statements on a CD, and we can immediately begin this disclosure. Another issue is other sensitive witnesses where we are -- where we asked to disclose their statements 30 days before from trial date. That is what we -- we want to wait, for securitive reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's one of the pending motions. Let me just see. I have to check. That's still a pending motion or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: There is one pending motion, our seventh motion for protective measures, and we are preparing an eighth motion for protective measures, which includes a delayed disclosure for sensitive witnesses and trial-related protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are allowed for the time being to wait what our decision will be on these motions before you -- before you disclose any material that is covered by those motions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Anything else to be added 66(A)(ii)? Then the next item on our disclosure list, Mr. Seselj, is Rule 68 material. I notice, Mr. Seselj, that in respect of Rule 68 material that there are although perhaps not strictly exculpatory material, that there are two issues pending, that is a motion you filed requesting all the material relating to the Serbian Guard to be disclosed to you. And another motion to compel certain states to disclose information. We'll soon deliver a decision on these motions, but there was a -- there were quite a lot of motions pending, so we have to do them one by one. Is there any matter the Prosecution would like to bring to my attention in relation to disclosure of Rule 68 material?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: There's nothing to add. It's more or less an ongoing procedure. We already disclosed something like 280.000 or we tried to disclose 280.000 pages which were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's mainly Rule 68(ii)?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's both the relevant material and exculpatory material, which I take it is not as vast in quantity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Yeah. And we also disclosed about 165 witness statements which mentioned the accused's name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's, to some extent, also covered by our disclosure decision of today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Seselj, would you like to raise any matter on the disclosure of Rule 68 material, which is under Rule 68(i), the exculpatory material, or under Rule 68(ii), other relevant material?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, you on the spot are brutally violating my rights pursuant to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The same legal value is attributed to submissions presented orally and written -- in written form, just like your rulings, whether they be oral or written. I have tabled a request for the Trial Chamber to enable me to complain and appeal your decision, and I have very strong reasons that I presented. And I expect the Trial Chamber to make a ruling in that regard. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I -- first of all, I invited you to make any submissions on the status of Rule 68 material. If you would insist me to give a decision on your request, I will do so. I gave you an opportunity to file it properly, but if you insist on a decision I will not only do it, but I'll give you the reasons for it right away. And I gave you a hint when I suggested to you to make such a request in writing. But again, tell me that you insist and I will give you the decision.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, I consider that I have already filed the request orally, and you do not have a right to give me a ruling straight away, because you cannot decide it as an individual. It is the Trial Chamber who makes a ruling and decision on that. You do not have the right to decide yourself here and now, and I do have the right to file an appeal orally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me do it the following way, Mr. Seselj. If you insist on having a decision at shortest notice, then the decision would certainly express, and I hinted to that at an earlier stage, that a request for a certificate for an appeal is to be denied unless the party presents the reasons for such a certificate, and these reasons for granting a certificate are found -- let me just have a look at what Rule it exactly is. In Rule 72 -- yes, Rule 73, I made a mistake. I was referring to preliminary motions. It's Rule 73, under (C) -- no, I am making a mistake. It's Rule 73 under (B) which reads: "Decisions on all motions are without interlocutory appeal save with certification by the Trial Chamber, which may grant such certification if the decision involves an issue that would significantly affect the fair and expeditious conduct of the proceedings or the outcome of the trial, and for which, in the opinion of the Trial Chamber, an immediate resolution by the Appeals Chamber may materially advance the proceedings." So I suggest to you that you elaborate in any request on these criteria you'll find in Rule 73(B). Then moving on. Is there anything, Mr. Seselj, you would like to say about the present status of Rule 68 material?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have you know that disclosure in electronic format means nothing to me unless I can pass it on to my legal advisors. On the one hand, you have forbidden me to provide them with material; and on the other, you provide me with useless computer diskettes. That is something that the jurisdiction has not seen yet; that is to say, to force the accused against his will to receive documents in electronic format. That is something that the judiciary and the history of the judiciary has never seen. And I'm grateful to you for that because my name will go down in the annals of world judiciary because you have done something that is quite unbelievable in my trial, so thank you very much for that, Mr. Orie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no need to thank me, Mr. Seselj. Then we move on to Rule 65 material. Pre-trial brief. The Prosecution has filed its pre-trial brief on the 14th of December, 2004, but due to the new amended, modified indictment which was filed on the 15th of July, 2005, an additional pre-trial brief covering greater Sarajevo, Bijeljina, Brcko, Mostar, and Nevesinje was filed on the 17th of February, 2006. Anything to be added in relation to the pre-trial brief under Rule 65 ter?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour, except for the fact that we also have filed a witness list and most recently the final exhibits list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I come to that, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff. The witness list was -- was recently updated and filing took place after it was translated on the 22nd of May; that was just a couple of days after the last Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the third item, the exhibits list. The exhibit list was submitted on the 17th of February, 2005 but was then filed only on the 14th of July, 2005, due to the need to be translated. Following the modified indictment, an updated exhibit list has been filed on the 3rd of July, yesterday, from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just passed a note for a moment because we actually brought down the materials on the 30th of June, 2006, but it was filed officially only yesterday. Yes, so you were right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I said the updated exhibit list has been filed yesterday. That's -- Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, could you tell us anything about the prospects for future disclosure in view of the decision on disclosure I just discussed already with you and of the denial of the certification to appeal a decision on protective measures which was issued on the 21st of June. Could you -- is there anything you would like to bring to my attention in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only -- the only thing that should be mentioned that in relation to the exhibits we of course will immediately disclose the exhibits as far as it -- these are not exhibits that are provided by sensitive witnesses where we had requested also delayed disclosure for these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I allowed you that not to include them in present disclosure until a decision has been taken on these requests.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Seselj, would you like to make any submissions, any observations, in relation to Rule 65 ter material? That is pre-trial brief, witness list, and exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday they tried to give me an exhibit list in the English language, and I refused that because I insist that this be exclusively done in the Serbian language. As for the witness list, I haven't received it yet. I received the pre-trial brief some two months ago, that is true. But, Mr. Orie, I received two expert reports and also the list of adjudicated facts. So I would like to tell you something about that. Anthony Oberschall and Yves Tomic are these experts. I am going to challenge all their allegations because these experts are highly unexpert-like, but I want to express my views in writing by the 1st of September. Also I need a deadline for writing about the adjudicated facts, too. I will give you a list of facts that are incorrect that I'm going to challenge and that are mentioned there as adjudicated facts. There are a great many incorrect facts that I will easily challenge. Unbelievable mistakes were made in terms of the facts themselves. So, if possible, could you give me the 1st of September as a deadline for all three, for Anthony Oberschall, Yves Thomas, and the list of adjudicated facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As far as the experts are concerned, you'll find the relevant Rule 94 bis where it says: "Within 30 days of disclosure of the statement of the expert witness, or such other time prescribed by the Trial Chamber or Pre-Trial Judge, the opposing party shall file a notice indicating whether: (i) it accepts the expert witness statement; or (ii) it wishes to cross-examine the expert witness; and (iii) it challenges the qualifications of the witness as an expert or the relevance of all or parts of the report and, if so, which parts." I do understand that you want to file such a notice. The Rules say that it should be done within 30 days, but also that the Trial Chamber or the Pre-Trial Judge could prescribe another time-limit. If you wait one second.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I may be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Because actually the accused may have forgotten it, but he has already filed a submission, number 141, related to the expert report of Anthony Oberschall, and it's dated the 17th of January, 2006, and we can easily -- sorry, that's when -- the official filing date is 24th of March, 2006, and I seem to recall that there is also already one for Mr. Tomic but that I need to check first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, could you please respond to that. First of all, it must have slipped out of my mind if it's there. But is it true that you filed already a --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm surprised, Mr. Orie, by what the Prosecutor said that I do remember this. I remember everything. I submitted it. It was one page respectively. I gave you notice that I'm going to challenge this and that I will want to question the expert as a witness. But in these filings I also asked for a deadline in order to carry out thorough preparations. So I stated my views as briefly as possible in a single sentence, but I want to prepare this seriously so that it could be obvious why I challenge what the expert said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, we'll check that, if you have asked within the time-limits for further time to prepare a filing -- prepare filing a notice under Rule 94 bis (B), and if no decision has been taken on that it is on the record now at least that you would like to have until the 1st of September.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, may I just add something else in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stated my views only with regard to items 1 and 2. Do I accept the expert witness statement? No. Do I wish to cross-examine the expert witness, yes, on both counts. And now number 3: Do I challenge the relevance -- or rather, the qualifications of the witness as an expert or the relevance of all or parts of the report? And if so, which parts. I have to do that very thoroughly. I have to indicate which parts and so on and so forth. Therefore, I need expert assistance. Not all of that can fit into one page. That is why I ask for this additional time, of course by your leave, although I have a right to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have in front of me a document which translates -- a handwritten document, Mr. Seselj, dated the 22nd of March, 2006, and I'll read it in full so to see whether there's any -- so that we are both aware, and the Prosecution, about its contents. It reads: "To Trial Chamber II. On the 21st of March, 2006, I received the Serbian translation of a document entitled 'Prosecution submission of the expert report of Anthony Oberschall, dated 17th January 2006. "I do not accept the report of the alleged expert because it is anti-Serbian, partial, politically biased, based on false assumptions and facts, and technically amateurish. I forcefully object to this report being included in the case file without testimony of the 'expert' in person. "I demand to be enabled to cross-examine Anthony Oberschall, within the court proceedings, about all the circumstances and the overall contents of his report. I shall contest Oberschall's overall report as well as every detail and the utterly inappropriate methodological procedure that was applied when drawing up this report." Mr. Seselj, upon reading this document, I have some difficulties to find a request for a further time-limit to be set by the Trial Chamber for making any further submissions under Rule 94 bis (B). Could you assist me where to find that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the submission where I stated my views on Yves Tomic, expert witness, I referred that I asked for the same treatment to be given to the Oberschall report, and obviously the Prosecutor had that in her hands. She seems to remember a bit of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I'm now focussing on the Oberschall report, and if in any Tomic document you ask for the same as you asked for in relation to Oberschall, then at least we should find a request in the Oberschall document. I can't read any request for setting of further time-limits here, but if it's somewhere else we'll certainly find and then -- Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- in our list of filings, there is no filing related to Mr. Tomic of that kind that we just spoke about in relation to Mr. Oberschall. Obviously I was mistaken with my memory. And also from what I see here, the Prosecution submitted the expert report under the filing date 23rd of May, 2006. So it is probably very doubtful that by now Mr. Seselj has the B/C/S version and could have filed a document like the one that he -- that you have now in hand in relation to Mr. Oberschall.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first try to make it clear when the Oberschall report was filed. Was that at that moment just in English or was it accompanied by a translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- Your Honour, I think Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you have misspoken. We are talking now about Tomic, are we not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I first wanted to come back to Oberschall.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oberschall was first filed in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And then after translation it was officially filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was at what date? I think that was on the 21st of March that Mr. Seselj received it --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's at least what he writes: "I received the Serbian translation of a document" --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And originally we filed the Oberschall report -- or, rather, we submitted the Oberschall report to the Registrar on the 17th of January, 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore, Mr. Seselj, up to this moment I have not found any request for a new time-limit to make any further submissions under Rule 94 bis under (B).

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to tell you two things. First of all, I'm astonished that the Prosecutor does not know what documents were submitted to me. On the 31st of May, 2006, I received in the Serbian language the report of expert Yves Tomic. And, Mr. Orie, in a submission on one page only, submission 172, I informed you -- please, that is less than one page. May I leave -- may I read, by your leave, what I said there? Do you allow me to do that, Mr. Orie?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you give me the date, I'll read what it says and see to what extent it is important.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 7th of June, 2006, submission 172, one page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll have a look. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Seselj, we'll verify whether it has been filed. Yes, but we now slowly move to the Tomic report. What would you like to bring to my attention, Mr. Seselj, in respect of the Tomic report and any submission under Rule 94 bis?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm presenting three positions here in this submission. Since I was never informed that the Trial Chamber or the representatives of the Judges set a deadline for disclosing any expert report called by the Prosecution, there is a dilemma as to Tomic's report is complete and whether it was submitted in due time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speaker is reading too fast. The interpreters cannot keep up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, if you don't slow down your speech, the interpreters will not be able to follow you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I'll slow down, Mr. Orie. I insist that I cross-examine the expert, and also I challenge his qualifications as an expert -- or rather, the relevance of the entire report. Since I fully challenge the entire report of Yves Tomic, Prosecution witness, and also his personal qualifications, and before that I also said to you that I challenge the report of Anthony Oberschall and his professional qualifications for that job, I require that Trial Chamber I should urgently clarify what this is all about, what deadlines are involved so that the members for my expert team for assisting the Defence could in a timely fashion give all the grounds for the challenge. As you told me that the trial will begin in the first half of October 2006, I ask that you set the 1st of September as a deadline by which I will give official notification as to why I do not accept the report by Anthony Oberschall and also the expert report of Yves Tomic. At the same time, these will be the reasons why I insist that both -- that I should cross-examine both expert witnesses and at the same time I will prove that neither of them is ethically credible or professionally qualified for the job entrusted to them by the Prosecution. Now I'm adding something to this orally, along similar lines. Again, I'm asking for the deadline of the 1st of September for the list of adjudicated facts so that I could tell you why I'm challenging the list of adjudicated facts and on what grounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just about to come to the adjudicated facts. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, one very practical question in relation to the report of Mr. Oberschall, the Defence -- or rather, Mr. Seselj has informed us that he does not accept the report. He did so on the 22nd of March where we writes -- of course that should be verified perhaps that he received the Serbian translation on the 21st of March, which means that under Rule 94 bis one would expect the expert witness to be called. Would you oppose against giving a deadline up till the 1st of September so that Mr. Seselj could challenge the qualifications of the witness as an expert or the relevance of the report as a whole or in part?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Despite the fact that Mr. Seselj has actually missed the deadlines given by the Rules, I wouldn't object against him filing his opinions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It might be a practical solution for that matter. It's always better that the parties and the Bench is aware of the reasons why Mr. Seselj challenges the qualifications of the witness. Mr. Seselj, it is not of great use to write down in full detail why you oppose the expert report. That's, of course, usually done at trial, but under Rule 94 bis you are expected to notify us whether you accept the report, whether you want to cross-examine the expert witness, and it's clear that you want to do that, and whether you challenge the qualifications and the relevance of this report. Mr. Seselj, we'll now move to the Tomic report. Could you tell us whether you asked for any further deadline to be set, apart from the deadline we find in Rule 94 bis under (B)?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, I did not ask for a deadline apart from a deadline because you actually never set a deadline for me. According to the Rules, the deadline is one month, and the Trial Chamber did not state its views in this regard. Now I'm asking the Trial Chamber to set a different deadline, as allowed by the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and the 1st of September would be an optimal deadline for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. Please, Mr. Seselj, be aware that the Rule reads that the deadline is 30 days or such other time prescribed by the Trial Chamber or the Pre-Trial Judge, which means that if no other time has been set as a deadline, that the 30 days of the Rule do apply. I have noted your request to get further time until the 1st of September. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, in relation to witness -- expert witness Tomic, any objection against this request?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- as I see it, the accused received the report end of May in his -- in the language he understands, and two months I think would be appropriate, because it is quite an extensive, complex report. So end of June -- end of July would actually be the date that we propose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you intend to call the expert witnesses early in the case or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, later on in the case. Thank you for that information. We'll consider the matter and we'll decide. We move on to the next item, that is 92 bis and adjudicated facts. Motions have been filed by the Office of the Prosecution. Mr. Seselj, you have replied orally with some remarks on 92 bis, that is written statements. I would like to inform the parties that for a number of reasons the Chamber has decided not to decide on the admission of these items until the beginning of the trial. Since this may well have an impact on the choice of evidence to be presented by the OTP, the Chamber wanted to notify the OTP of this as soon as -- this to the parties as soon as possible. Also this means that the Chamber allows the accused to respond to these submissions - and we're now talking, Mr. Seselj, about adjudicated facts and 92 bis material - until the 15th of August, that is six weeks from now on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, I never received any 92 bis material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I do understand that this 92 bis material was offered electronically.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not true. It was offered in the English language, 14 enormous binders, on paper but in English. It is not true that it was in Serbian in electronic form. Of course I would have refused electronic form, too, but that's not true. It was on paper in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that it was an audio -- or could you please --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, what we did is we made simply a usual filing with the Rule 92 bis materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And usually the Registrar would then translate the documentation. And our proposal to the Registrar was to provide audio files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And -- but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which has been practiced many times in this, especially if it is Rule 92 bis (D) material from --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I assume so. But -- but I'm not sure whether this was actually then done by the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- we'll --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: At least what I know is that Mr. Seselj returned the filing completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll try to find out exactly what happened, whether it has been considered to provide --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Seselj, let me just finish my sentence before I allow you to speak. We'll find out what exactly happened. But was it ever suggested to you whether or not you liked that suggestion that the 92 bis material would be provided to you apart from in hard copy in English in audio material?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. As for what the Prosecutor said a few moments ago, that's not true. I did not return the entire material; I returned only what was in English, and that is an enormous quantity, 95 per cent, but I selected everything that was in Serbian and kept that. And I sent an accompanying letter on five handwritten pages to the Prosecutor, and I referred exactly to what I kept and what I'm returning. And I'm returning it because it's in English. Mr. Orie, methods are being devised here all the time in order to impede my preparation for defence. Now audio material. One man cannot listen to all of that. This material has to be on paper. With all these slow translators, very often unprofessional ones, what am I supposed to do? Spend a year listening to all the material they're going to submit to me? Imagine how many hours that is going to be and how many hours per day a person can spend fully focussed on listening to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, if you have any complaints about translations, you may make submissions on that. General statements on slow translators and general statements on unqualified translators are not appreciated. Please draw our attention to any specific complaints where you consider a translation to be not correct, as you did in the past a couple of times. We'll -- so when you said you do not have 92 bis material, you never received any 92 bis material, I now understand that you kept a small portion of it and you returned whatever was in English --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that's at least then clear for the time being. We'll further look into the matter to see what has happened and what still has to be done in this respect. It goes without saying that if the result of such inquiries would justify a new deadline to be set, so that is not the 15th of August but later, then a decision will be taken accordingly. Anything else on 92 bis material? If not, we move to adjudicated facts. Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say something about adjudicated facts, Mr. Orie, or have we gone through that? The material that was -- I was provided with and the adjudicated facts, I have received that with the additional material. And it is some 75 pages of an addendum and 418 facts. Now, I have already pin-pointed the ones that I intend to challenge of those 418, and I am going to do that in writing of course with the help of my expert team. If you allow me the 1st of September deadline, I can get through that work by that time. But I haven't had time to write it yet because I received the material on the 29th of June. But I have pin-pointed everything that I intend to challenge, and you can take a look at that if you're interested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although I said the 15th of August as a deadline, I'll consider whether we would allow you until the 1st of September, which would then be the same date as the dates for the two expert reports. Mr. Seselj, perhaps it's unnecessary to tell you, but when you are making submissions as to the admission of adjudicated facts, then it might be a good idea to orient yourself and to focus on the criteria which are accepted in the case law of this Tribunal for the acceptance of -- for the admission of adjudicated facts. I just -- without giving an exhaustive list, I just mention, for example, that this should be facts rather than legal findings, that these should be facts that are not established on the basis of any plea agreement, that should be facts that are finally established in a final decision. That means that if a decision is still pending on appeal, the facts established in the first instance could not be taking judicial notice of as adjudicated facts until the Appeals Chamber has decided or - and that's another exception - if they are not challenged on the appeal. So therefore, if you want to challenge them -- of course if you say: I do not agree them to be admitted, these are the kind of criteria the Chamber will first of all take into account. But even if an adjudicated fact has been taken judicial notice of, at least where they are admitted so that judicial notice can be taken of them, there still is an opportunity, although within certain limits, to prove that these adjudicated facts which do not require proof anymore are nevertheless not facts in the real sense of the word. So therefore, please focus on the criteria under Rule 94 to start with, and if you find at any moment once they are admitted any reason to challenge these facts which do not require proof then anymore, then that would be the moment to present evidence on these facts. Anything else on 92 bis and adjudicated facts? Yes, then we move on to the next one -- yes, yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, I do not intend to challenge the factual context of concrete crimes from other trials and proceedings, because those crimes have nothing to do with the indictment against me. But I do intend to challenge the facts that have to do with general historical and political circumstances; they are untruthful. And I have come by the knowledge, because I have read all the judgements that are available in the Serbian language, that the Defence in most cases never dealt with those questions. It wasn't interested in dealing with those matters, so cardinal errors slipped through, historical falsifications, if I can put it that way. And that is something I find totally unacceptable, so I would like to state my views on each and every fact. As I say, I'm not interested on specific crimes in other proceedings and trials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, we'll read in your submissions what adjudicated facts you're challenging and which not, and I do understand that one of the criteria that might be of importance for you is whether they are fully litigated, yes or no. Then we move on to the next item on the agenda. I would like to deliver an oral decision. That is the decision on the accused's motion requesting the Trial Chamber to acquire a complete report on the accused's health. This is a decision on the accused's submission number 159 entitled: Motion for Trial Chamber I to acquire a complete report on the health of Professor Vojislav Seselj. The accused's submission, dated the 19th of May, 2006, requests that the Trial Chamber instruct the Registry to provide copies of the accused's complete health report to the Trial Chamber and to the accused. The accused submits that on the 25th of April, 2006, when his wife came to the United Nations Detention Unit for a visit, she was required to sign a form entitled: Undertaking for visitors, in which she undertook not to disclose information about the accused's health to anyone. He submits that such restrictions regarding his health information indicate that the Registry has knowledge of a deteriorating medical condition of which he himself is unaware. The accused thus requests copies of his complete medical report. On the 8th of June, 2006, Mr. Sebastian van de Vliet, head of the office for legal aid and detention matters, sent a letter to the accused explaining that his wife was required to sign the undertaking for visitors form because of her interview appearing in the 12th of April, 2006 edition of the Nedeljni Telegraf, in which she discussed information regarding, and I quote from the letter: "The security screening procedures at the United Nations Detention Unit, the location of detainees within the United Nations Detention Unit, and information concerning other United Nations Detention Unit detainees." The letter also informed the accused that the Registry had taken his complaint into consideration and the language of the visitors' form regarding the health information of the accused persons being visited had been changed. The form now no longer contains any general prohibition on the disclosure of the health information of the accused person being visited. On the 29th of June, 2006, the Registry filed a submission with the Trial Chamber explaining that requiring the accused's wife to sign the visitor form was an appropriate restriction designed to protect the interests of security and good order at the United Nations Detention Unit given the accused's wife's disclosure to the media of sensitive information concerning UNDU procedures. The Registry also submits, and I quote: "It does not consider the accused's medical condition to be in such a state that a report needs to be filed before the Trial Chamber." On the 28th of June, 2006, the Prosecution filed its response to the accused's submission number 159. It submits that the accused has failed to show any medical justification for the production of a complete medical report or how acquiring such a report would facilitate the preparation or conduct of the trial, or serve the interests of justice. The Prosecution also submits that the accused's complaint was improperly filed with the Trial Chamber instead of with the Registrar and the President of the Tribunal. The Prosecution requests that the submission be denied. The Trial Chamber notes that the Registry required the accused's wife to sign the undertaking for visitors form because of her interview with the media in which she disclosed information regarding the security and the detention practices of the UNDU. The Trial Chamber considers that the specific restriction regarding the non-disclosure of the accused's health information was part of the general requirements of the undertaking for visitors form and was not specifically imposed in response to a deteriorating medical condition of the accused. The Trial Chamber further notes that since the filing of the accused's submission, the Registry has adjusted the language of the visitor form to accommodate the accused's concerns. Finally, the Trial Chamber considers that the legal remedy sought, namely the production of a complete medical report on the health status of the accused, has no basis given that the Registry is not aware of a deteriorating medical condition of the accused requiring the attention of the Trial Chamber. The Trial Chamber therefore denies the accused's request, and this concludes the Trial Chamber's decision. Then I'd like to invite the parties to tell me whether there are any other matters to be raised. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have some -- one small matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On the 28th of March this year, we actually provided to the Registrar the -- a motion for the -- to the Trial Chamber which was then actually filed on the 31st March 2006 concerning the filing of the expert report of Mr. Theunens, the military expert. We had requested the Trial Chamber to allow us to file a redacted version of this report, and we were wondering when a decision is made on our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll look into the matter. I couldn't give you an answer right away, but thank you for drawing your attention to this motion still pending. We are trying to get the list of pending motions down in number as soon as possible, but there is quite a lot of work to be done as you well understand. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, any matter to be raised on your part?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. According to the instructions with respect to the length of filings, Mr. Orie, the party who wishes the Trial Chamber to allow it to have a more lengthy filing must submit a request to that effect. However, when the Prosecution filed a request to impose counsel on me, it did not seek permission beforehand but in the text of the request stated why it considers the filing and motion should be longer than the one prescribed. When I responded to that filing, different criteria were applied to me, and my response was returned, although it was much shorter than the Prosecution filing and did not go beyond 3.000 pages. Because when I counted, I counted 4.545 words. Your staff did not count the words. It would appear that my 29th of May filing has less than 3.000 words, but you returned it, whereas you didn't return the Prosecution's filing, although it did not request in advance to allow it to submit its filing on more pages than allowed. From that, Mr. Orie, I draw the conclusion just how biased you are and in favour of the Prosecution to my disadvantage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, we'll look into that matter. The Chamber has not decided yet on the motion. At the same time, I can inform you that if rules are not observed in full and exceptionally there is a non full observance of that rule, then Chambers are inclined to show more flexibility compared to situations where, as the decision reads, and I'll read the most important line of it perhaps again, that in a situation as the Chamber considered that for reasons of the prolixity of the submissions you filed, Mr. Seselj, that patent lack of merit in general, their repetitiousness of their arguments and the triviality of most of the issues raised where -- for these reasons the Chamber considered that you had abused the process of the court less flexibility might be inclined to be given. At the same time, I do understand that you insist that at least your request that we pay more attention to any filing by the OTP going beyond the page limit, the general page limit which is applicable, that you suggest to us that we should not accept any filing which goes beyond such a limit without prior approval. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just looking at our filing and it says, actually, in paragraph 3 of this filing, which indeed is about 4.500 words long, it says: "The Prosecution seeks authorisation from the Trial Chamber to exceed the word limits."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, I think the issue raised by Mr. Seselj is that you should first ask for exceeding the page limit and only once leave is granted that you would be allowed to file a submission that goes beyond that page limit. That's the point I take it, Mr. Seselj, that you would like to bring to my attention; is that correct? I'll consider the matter with the other Judges of the Chamber and pay proper attention to it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have something to add, Mr. Orie. In this submission, in one point of it, I state, because I know that permission should be asked in advance, and I'm interpreting this in a freer form, that permission be asked in advance. So if the Prosecution didn't ask in advance, I'm not asking either. I'm asking it in my -- in my response to the Prosecution. But you returned my response, whereas you accepted the Prosecution's. Now, when you speak of triviality, you are not applying the same criteria. According to one criteria, you say that my filings and submissions are trivial, and you use another yard-stick and criterion to allow the Prosecution to supply me with an enormous amount of trivial material under Rule 68, just as the reports about the exhumation of bodies in the Prijedor area that I referred to last time. So those aren't trivialities, are they, and what I'm writing about are trivialities? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, the only thing I did is to quote from the decision on the length of your submissions, and in order to explain where Chambers are more or less inclined to show some flexibility, that's the only thing I did. And I did not initiate any debate on what is and what is not trivial in submissions by the parties in more general terms. Anything else, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I also would like to note, Mr. Orie, that in that way you are demonstrating your breadth of vision towards one side and your lack of it towards the other side; that is to say, you're not adhering to the rules. Either rules apply to one and all, or you can change them according to your own free will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, this is not a debating club in which we are going to enter into a debate. I invited you, as a matter of fact, whether there was any other issue, not continuing the same issue, to be raised.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This was an additional issue, Mr. Orie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Seselj. Mr. Van der Spoel, anything to be raised? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then this concludes this Status Conference --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, yes, I do have something to say. I have a short objection, Mr. Orie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Make your --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was an error in the interpretation -- or rather, the translator. Because van der Spoel was not -- you can say that he's a stand-by counsel, but he's not a counsel of mine, Defence counsel in any way. I have made that decision definite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the beginning of this session I established that stand-by counsel, Mr. Van der Spoel, was present, and I addressed him at the very end of this session as "Mr. Van der Spoel." That's on the record as far as I'm concerned. This concludes this Status Conference. We stand adjourned sine die.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: adjourned at 6.26 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
